program_name: Molecular Biotechnology (official English name; full title used on the programme microsite: 'Master Program in Molecular Biotechnology'. Italian official name: 'Biotecnologie Molecolari'. UNITO internal degree-programme code [0101M23]; apply.unito.it course id 393; unito.it degree id 29350). Run by the Department of Molecular Biotechnology and Health Sciences (Dipartimento di Biotecnologie Molecolari e Scienze per la Salute, DBMSS), School of Medicine.
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale). apply.unito.it lists 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time'; nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS. For each year of enrolment students may choose full-time or part-time status, with tuition adjusted accordingly.
teaching_language: Case 1 - fully English-taught. The whole degree is delivered in English; apply.unito.it lists 'Study language: English' and the UNITO catalogue lists the teaching language as English. It is a single-university UNITO degree (Department of Molecular Biotechnology and Health Sciences) - NOT an interuniversity/joint degree and NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree. The programme is internally structured into two curricula - MCTB (Molecular Computational and Translational Biotechnology) and BIDD (Biomedical Imaging and Drug Discovery) - but both are taught in English, so the curriculum choice does not change the language of instruction. No Italian-language requirement is published for admission or graduation. The programme is also open to students of the BioHealth Computing EM (Erasmus Mundus / EU Master) programme coming from worldwide, which is an incoming-mobility arrangement rather than a joint-degree structure. [uncertain - the exact current curriculum names could not be re-verified on a live official page; they come from the programme's Study Plan / Schedule pages via search snippets]
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy. apply.unito.it: 'Study location: Italy, Turin'. Department: Department of Molecular Biotechnology and Health Sciences (DBMSS), Via Nizza 52 area / UNITO central address Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino. School: School of Medicine (Scuola di Medicina). Programme office telephone 011 670 6416, e-mail segdid.biotecmol@unito.it.
degree_class: LM-9 - Biotecnologie mediche, veterinarie e farmaceutiche (Medical, Veterinary and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies). UNITO internal programme code: [0101M23]. 120 ECTS over 2 years.
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero) WITH a compulsory qualifying admission test. The programme's own page states: 'The Master program in Molecular Biotechnology is a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places. However, candidates are subjected to a preliminary verification of the specific curricular and personal requirements.' There is no numerus clausus ranking and no TOLC, SAT, GRE or GMAT. Instead there is a programme-specific written verification test (multiple-choice, held online) that must be passed with a score of at least 60% in order to enrol. Two application routes exist: (a) applicants holding a FOREIGN degree (any citizenship) apply through the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 393); (b) applicants holding an ITALIAN Bachelor degree apply through MyUniTo using 'Iscrizioni > Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero'. A territorial cap applies only to one group: 50 places are reserved for non-European applicants residing abroad. Italian graduates of class L-2 (Biotechnology) or L-13 (Biological Sciences) with a final mark of at least 102/110 are exempt from the verification test.
application_deadline_eu: A.Y. 2026/27: 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time - the Fourth admission call on Apply@UniTo (25 August - 8 September 2026), which is the call for open-access postgraduate degree programmes and is 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy'. apply.unito.it course 393 shows exactly this deadline. EU applicants with a foreign degree may alternatively use the earlier First admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), which is open to all applicants. Applicants holding an ITALIAN Bachelor degree do not use Apply@UniTo: they pre-enrol through MyUniTo within the programme's own domestic window (in the 2024/25 cycle this ran 1 July - 2 September 2024, 15:00); the equivalent 2026/27 domestic window was not readable on a live official page [uncertain - only the domestic MyUniTo window is uncertain; the 8 September 2026 Apply@UniTo deadline is directly verified on the course page]. Separately, the admission/verification test date for 2026/27 is 16 September 2026, and the enrolment deadline for candidates who had not yet graduated at application time falls in mid-January of the following year (17 January 2025, 15:00 in the 2024/25 cycle).
application_deadline_non_eu: A.Y. 2026/27: 29 January 2026 - non-EU applicants residing abroad must apply through Apply@UniTo in the First admission call (25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026), which is the only 2026/27 call described as 'open to all applicants wishing to apply for postgraduate degree programs'. The later Fourth call closing 8 September 2026 is explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy', and apply.unito.it warns: 'If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' Successful non-EU applicants must additionally complete visa pre-enrolment on the Universitaly platform by the national/UNITO deadline (15 July 2026 was reported for the 2026/27 UNITO cycle), which is not stated on this programme's own pages. entry_exam_or_test: YES - a programme-specific written VERIFICATION TEST (admission test), held remotely/online. apply.unito.it states: 'Personal preparation of the candidates will be verified by a written test (held via web).' The programme's Test page states: 'Verification test will be held remotely on Wednesday September 16th 2026 at 11 a.m.' (the archived 2025/26 version of the same page read 'Tuesday September 16th 2025 at 11 a.m.', confirming the page is updated each cycle). Format: 'The test is designed to assess your knowledge in Biology and Chemistry and it is divided in two areas: Area 1 - Biology includes 30 multiple-choice questions on the following disciplines: Cellular Biology, Molecular Biology, Genetics. Area 2 - Chemistry includes 30 multiple-choice questions on the following disciplines: Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry. Four proposed answers are given for every question. Candidates can mark only ONE answer. All questions carry equal marks. No marks will be deducted for wrong answers. Time for each area is 30 minutes.' Pass mark: 'A positive score (>= 60%) is required to be enrolled in the Master Program in Molecular Biotechnology.' Total: 60 multiple-choice questions, 60 minutes. Detailed instructions are published as a PDF: https://www.molecularbiotechnology.unito.it/att/Instructions_admission_test.pdf . EXEMPTION: 'Candidates holding an Italian Bachelor Degree in either Biotechnology (class L2) or Biological Sciences (class L13) obtained with a final score above or equal to 102/110 are exempt from the verification test.' There is NO interview and NO standardised external test (no TOLC, SAT, GRE, GMAT). [uncertain - the 16 September 2026 date and weekday come from live search-engine renderings of the Test page; the microsite host itself was unreachable and the Wayback snapshot still carried the 2025 date]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION: a Bachelor degree (three-year first-level degree) obtained in Italy (DM 509 or DM 270) or an equivalent/higher qualification obtained from a foreign university. apply.unito.it: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education.' Candidates who do not yet hold the degree at the date of application are accepted ('We accept also candidates not yet holding a Bachelor Degree at the date of application'), but must obtain it by the enrolment deadline (in the 2024/25 cycle: 17 January 2025, 15:00).

DISCIPLINARY BACKGROUND (eligibility criteria, from the programme's Admission Requirements page):
- An Italian Bachelor degree in class L-2 (Biotechnology) or class L-13 (Biological Sciences), OR another Italian Bachelor degree 'providing a solid background in General and Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics'.
- To be admitted to the verification test, candidates holding an ITALIAN Bachelor degree must have at least: 50 credits (CFU) in one or more of the scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) BIO/01, BIO/05, BIO/06, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/13, BIO/14, BIO/16, BIO/17, BIO/18, BIO/19, CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/08; AND 10 credits in one or more of the SSDs FIS/01-FIS/08, MAT/01-MAT/09, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, MED/01, INF/01.
- Candidates holding a degree obtained from a FOREIGN university must have 'an appropriate number of credits in the following subjects: Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, General and Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics' (no numeric CFU figure is published for foreign degrees on the microsite).
- apply.unito.it renders the same requirement for its (foreign-degree) applicant pool in a stricter, countable form: 'a solid background certified by at least 8 exams passed in the following subjects: Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, General and Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics.'

MINIMUM GRADE: apply.unito.it states 'Furthermore, applicants must hold an undergraduate degree with a grade equal to or exceeding 9.3/10 of the highest possible grade (102/110 for an Italian degree).' On the programme microsite the same 102/110 threshold appears only as an EXEMPTION rule from the verification test for Italian L-2/L-13 graduates, not as a universal minimum. Treat 102/110 (9.3/10) as a hard minimum for Apply@UniTo (foreign-degree) applicants. [uncertain - the two official sources use the same number for different purposes]

OTHER PREREQUISITES: 'Basic computer skills (Microsoft office, internet navigation)' and English at CEFR B2 (see language_requirements).

QUOTA / PLACES: no overall numerus clausus - 'a postgraduate degree without a restricted number of places'. The only published cap is territorial: apply.unito.it, 'Territory requirements: This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.' No EU sub-quota and no total intake figure is published.

STRUCTURE: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time or part-time by yearly election; two curricula (MCTB - Molecular Computational and Translational Biotechnology; BIDD - Biomedical Imaging and Drug Discovery); heavy laboratory/internship component, with most of the formative curriculum spent on experimental work in a research laboratory.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH ONLY - no Italian language requirement is published (the degree is fully English-taught). Required level: CEFR B2. The programme's Admission Requirements page: 'a minimum B2 English language level under the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR)'.

Unlike most UNITO programmes, this one publishes an explicit ACCEPTED-CERTIFICATE LIST WITH MINIMUM SCORES on apply.unito.it: 'Applicants must hold an international certification (see footnote for list of accepted certifications and minimum scores requirements), certifying at least a CEFR B2 level of English language proficiency. Language certification must be no more than three years old.' Accepted certifications and minimum scores:
- Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) - no minimum score stated (C2)
- Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) - no minimum score stated (C1)
- Cambridge First Certificate of English (FCE) - minimum score 173 (grade B)
- PTE Academic - minimum score 65
- IELTS - minimum 5.5 out of 9, with no component lower than 5.5
- TOEFL iBT - minimum 69 out of 120, with no component lower than 17
- Trinity College ISE II

VALIDITY: the certificate must be no more than three years old.
No exemption rule (e.g. for native speakers or for a prior degree taught entirely in English) is published on any accessible official page for this programme. Applicants with an Italian Bachelor degree submit instead 'a self-declaration of knowledge about computer skills and English language' through MyUniTo, i.e. the domestic route uses self-certification rather than an international certificate. [uncertain - no published exemption rule; the domestic self-declaration route contrasts with the strict certificate list applied to Apply@UniTo applicants]
required_documents:
A) APPLICANTS WITH A FOREIGN DEGREE - via the Apply@UniTo portal (apply.unito.it, course 393):
1. Valid identity document / passport (passport for non-EU citizens).
2. First-cycle (bachelor's) degree certificate obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or an equivalent/higher qualification. If not yet awarded, evidence that it will be obtained by the enrolment deadline.
3. Official academic transcript of records with exams, credits (CFU/ECTS) and grades, so that the '8 exams passed' subject requirement and the 9.3/10 (102/110) minimum final grade can be verified.
4. MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian - explicitly required ('Other requirements: A motivation letter must be added to your application'); Apply@UniTo also lists the motivation letter as mandatory for all postgraduate programmes.
5. English language certificate at CEFR B2 or above from the accepted list (CPE / CAE / FCE 173 B / PTE Academic 65 / IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 69 / Trinity ISE II), issued no more than three years before application.
6. Optional but recommended: degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish.
7. Payment of the non-refundable EUR 60 application fee within the deadline of the call (same amount whether one or two degree programmes are selected).
LANGUAGE OF DOCUMENTS: 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'
AFTER SUBMISSION: UNITO may request further documents such as a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore), a Statement of Verification, or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability; the International Students Office may request additional documentation again at the enrolment stage.

B) APPLICANTS WITH AN ITALIAN BACHELOR DEGREE - via MyUniTo ('Iscrizioni > Pre-iscrizione ai corsi ad accesso libero'), per the programme's How to apply page:
1. Copy of Identity Card / Passport / Driving Licence.
2. A self-certification attesting a first-level degree with exams OR, for candidates expected to graduate, a self-certification attesting enrolment in the undergraduate degree with passed exams.
3. A self-declaration of knowledge about computer skills and English language.
4. Course syllabus - only for candidates graduated or expected to graduate in degree classes other than L-2 (Biotechnology) or L-13 (Biological Sciences).

C) ALL CANDIDATES (unless exempt): sit the online verification test on the published date and score at least 60%.
[uncertain - list B and its submission window were read from the 2024/25 version of the How to apply page (last update 09/07/2024); the 2026/27 version could not be read on a live official page]
